findings.breaking_input: The Neon account already has a project named arc-launch-<slug> that the owner made, and the board's state records no neon-project (`recorded` is empty). scaffold finds one hit, so `id` is set. The guard `id && !recorded.includes(id) && recorded.length` is false because `recorded.length` is 0. The owner's project is adopted, `ctx.report` records it as launch's, and the migration runs against it.
findings.why: The foreign-project refusal only fires when something else is already recorded, so the first run adopts any same-named project. Teardown then deletes it, and the migration writes into the owner's database. This is a twin of 'A project and domain launch only found were recorded as launch's' and 'report the CREATE, not the check'. The `foreign` fake scenario is never run in the bats arms, so nothing covers this.
findings.fix: Refuse any found project that is not in `recorded`, whatever `recorded.length` is. Report only a project this call created, or one already recorded. Add a `foreign` arm to the contract bats test.
findings.twin_of: A project and domain launch only found were recorded as launch's, so teardown would delete the owner's -> every check-then-create: report the CREATE, not the check

findings.breaking_input: The owner's Neon project (or one already holding the owner's data) has its own public.launch_probe table with other columns or rows. MIGRATION runs `create table if not exists`, `alter table ... enable row level security`, then inserts id 1.
findings.why: It alters and writes to a table launch did not create, because the name is one the owner can also use. Verify's `owner_rows == 1` check also fails whenever the owner's table has more rows.
findings.fix: Use a launch-unique table name carrying an ownership marker, or refuse if the table already exists without a marker comment.
findings.twin_of: A probe table of the same name as the owner's was altered and written to -> every create-if-not-exists on a name the owner can also use

findings.breaking_input: `verify --all --public-only` hits a slot whose adapter drifted (DIGEST_DRIFT) or that is otherwise UNVERIFIABLE. The catch branch logs it and does `failed++; continue`, which never reaches the `incident.raised` emit. The run returns exit 1.
findings.why: launch-watch treats exit 1 as 'a regression the runner already raised to needs-you', so a drifted or unverifiable slot gets no incident and the watch reports success. The weekly watch is silent on the case it should catch.
findings.fix: In public-only mode, emit `incident.raised` on the UNVERIFIABLE path too. Have launch-watch distinguish exit 1 with raised incidents from exit 1 without any.

findings.breaking_input: One board's verify times out at 3600s, or the child is killed. On Windows a SIGKILLed child reports status 1, and `r.signal` and `r.error` are never read.
findings.why: A timeout looks like exit 1, so it is treated as an already-raised regression and `failed` stays 0. The job exits 0 and writes the stamp. The cause is inferred from `status` alone.
findings.fix: Check `r.error`, `r.signal` and `r.status === null` before interpreting the exit code. Count a timeout or kill as failed.
findings.twin_of: Windows reports a SIGKILLed child as plain exit 1, so a reason built from the exit code named the wrong cause

findings.breaking_input: Any run in which a board's verify fails, or a board is skipped. `writeFileSync(STAMP, today)` runs unconditionally after the loop.
findings.why: A failed watch still marks the week done, so the retry waits seven days. Each venture's timeout is 3600s against a job budget of min 30. If the runner kills the job mid-loop no stamp is written, and the first sorted slugs starve the later ones every day.
findings.fix: Write the stamp only when `failed === 0`. Track per-board progress, and cap the per-venture timeout below the job budget.

findings.breaking_input: A `.watch-last` holding a future date, such as `2099-01-01` from a clock skew or a hand edit. `daysBetween(last, today)` is negative, so `< 7` is true.
findings.why: The stamp is trusted without a bound, so the watch skips indefinitely, and the printed message claims 'next on or after N more day(s)' with a huge number.
findings.fix: Treat a stamp in the future as absent, i.e. require `0 <= days < 7`.

findings.breaking_input: hq.policy.yaml checked out with CRLF line endings on Windows. ANCHOR ends with a bare `\n`, so `policy.includes(ANCHOR)` is false and the script exits 2 with 'add the block by hand'. Without that failure, BLOCK and ROW would be written with LF into a CRLF file.
findings.why: The owner's one-line apply fails on the owner's own OS, and an apply that succeeded would leave mixed line endings. No shared-file edit reads the file's own conventions first.
findings.fix: Detect the file's EOL and convert BLOCK and ROW to it. Match the anchor with `\r?\n`.
findings.twin_of: `.env.example` names were matched without `export ` and added with LF into a CRLF file -> every shared-file edit: read the file's own conventions first

findings.breaking_input: A profile with `repository: "--dry-run"`, or any value starting with `--`, passed as the argv value after `--repository`. venture-register may treat it as a flag.
findings.why: The user-supplied profile string goes into a child's argv with no format check. `spawnSync` also blocks the worker's event loop for up to 120s, so the slot's abort timeout cannot fire. On Windows a SIGKILL timeout reports exit 1, which is then named 'exited 1'.
findings.fix: Validate `repository` against `^[\w.-]+/[\w.-]+$`. Use an async spawn so the abort signal is honoured, and check `r.signal` and `r.error`.
findings.twin_of: Windows reports a SIGKILLed child as plain exit 1, so a reason built from the exit code named the wrong cause

findings.breaking_input: A verify adapter returns `reason: "PAUSED(x)"` or `"env:K"` for a slot that has really regressed.
findings.why: With `--public-only` the incident is suppressed purely on an adapter-supplied reason prefix. A broken or hostile adapter (or any reason built from a response body) silences its own regression. `PAUSED(` is accepted from free text and not from a typed field.
findings.fix: Have adapters return a typed `status` field (`paused` or `env`) and validate it. Do not match a prefix of free text.

findings.breaking_input:
A Windows checkout where the adapter files are already CRLF. `bytes.replace(/
/g, "
")` turns each `
` into `
`.
findings.why: The 'CRLF keeps digest' check feeds a double-CR copy to the digest. If adapterDigest only folds `\r\n`, `crlfSame` is false on the autocrlf leg only. The test edits checked-out text without normalising first.
findings.fix:
Normalise with `bytes.replace(/
/g, "
").replace(/
/g, "
")` before writing the CRLF copy.
findings.twin_of: The lint self-test edited LF literals into files a Windows checkout gives it as CRLF -> every test fixture that edits checked-out text by literal match

findings.breaking_input: The fixture registry.yaml checked out with CRLF, or missing a trailing newline. `add_probe_rows` appends LF rows with `printf >>` after grepping the first digest with awk, so `$d` can end in `\r`.
findings.why: The `digest:` value read from a CRLF file carries a CR, so the appended rows get a corrupt digest and the registry gets mixed EOLs. The test fails on the Windows leg only.
findings.fix: Strip CR from `$d` with `tr -d '\r'`, and append through a helper that matches the file's EOL.
findings.twin_of: Two bats fixtures edited a checked-out YAML with a sed `$` anchor that misses on a CRLF line
